summary: End-to-end review of Crypto Agility + Federated Key Registry + Bring-Your-Own-Signing on iteration 17. Backend: 9/9 pytest cases passed against the public REACT_APP_BACKEND_URL — backward-compat default Ed25519, ES256/ES256K via signature_suite, unknown suite rejected with HTTP 400, /api/demo/issue + GET /api/demo/verify/{proof_id} valid=true, /api/demo/artifact + /api/demo/artifact/verify valid=true, federated key register (status=pending + pop_challenge) → bad PoP HTTP 400 → good PoP confirm (status=active, pop_verified=true) and key listed in /api/public/keys with owner=partner, BYOS local ES256 signer changes per-tenant signing algorithm from Ed25519 → ES256 and /api/admin/signers/health.default_signer.available=true, /api/developer.signing exposes signature_suites.supported=[Ed25519,ES256,ES256K] and crypto_agility/federated_keys/byos.enabled=true. Sandbox signer was deleted at teardown — final /api/admin/signers list is empty so demo portal stays on Ed25519. Frontend: /developers Trust & Cryptographic Architecture badges (Crypto Agility, Federated Key Registry, Bring-Your-Own-Signing) all render with ES256/ES256K listed; /docs/crypto-agility loads with 19 headings + 5 tables and the sidebar exposes 3 'Crypto Agility' links (under Architecture and Security & Trust); admin/login → /admin dashboard works with admin@pfprotocol.com/PfpAdmin!2026; demo portal '/' still renders the Generic Workflow Builder.
critical_code_review_comments: Review_request text says 'POST /api/admin/signers?tenant_id=sandbox' to BYOS-flip the sandbox-key flow, but the sandbox API key (SANDBOX_API_KEY) is bound to the DEFAULT_TENANT_ID='default' tenant in backend/.env + api_key_service.ensure_sandbox_key. Configuring a signer on tenant_id=sandbox does NOT affect sandbox-key FEA generation; you must use tenant_id=default. Behavior is correct (tenant-scoped); only the review_request wording is misleading. Consider either (a) creating a dedicated 'sandbox' tenant and binding the sandbox key to it, or (b) updating docs/tests to reflect tenant_id=default. Test now uses tenant_id=default.

Frontend TrustArchitecture.jsx labels feature status as 'Active' (e.g., {label:'Federated Key Registry', status:'Active'}) rather than an 'Available today' column. The badges/content all render correctly; if the marketing copy is supposed to be 'Available today' per the spec, update TrustArchitecture.jsx — otherwise the spec wording is just approximate.

ECDSA low-S enforcement and raw r||s (64B) encoding are exercised end-to-end and public verify returns signature_valid=true for both ES256 and ES256K — algorithm binding in verify_fea correctly accepts the suite recorded in payload.algorithm.
Idempotency key is required on POST /api/fea/generate — request schema validation is strict (good); make sure SDKs/clients always include it (the SDK parity tests already do).

Federated register response uses field name 'public_key_id' (not 'key_id'). The /confirm body also uses 'public_key_id'. This is internally consistent but slightly differs from the review_request wording (which said 'key_id'). No code change needed; doc/wording only.
seed_data_creation: Test creates TEST_-prefixed FEAs (via /api/fea/generate), one federated Ed25519 partner key (PoP-confirmed, persists in DB as label='TEST_FED_KEY'), and TEST_ demo proofs. BYOS signer on tenant=default is created and DELETED in the test teardown — verified post-run /api/admin/signers returns total=0.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Backend e2e suite is /app/backend/tests/test_crypto_review_e2e.py (9 tests, all green, ~3.5s) and the JUnit XML is /app/test_reports/pytest/crypto_review_results.xml. The sandbox API key resolves to tenant 'default' — when testing BYOS or tenant-scoped behavior with the sandbox key, use tenant_id=default in admin endpoints. /api/demo/verify/{proof_id} is GET, not POST. /api/demo/artifact returns the raw signed artifact JSON (not wrapped in {artifact:...}); pass it directly to /api/demo/artifact/verify. Federated register/confirm both use field 'public_key_id'. PoP message is exactly ('PFP_POP_V1::' + challenge).encode() signed with PyNaCl SigningKey, base64-encoded. /api/developer 'signing' block is at the top level (data.signing). The 'sandbox' signer in /api/admin/signers/health is expected after a successful BYOS test only if not cleaned up — current state is clean.
rca of the issue: n/a — no defects found. The only friction was a wording mismatch between review_request (tenant_id=sandbox) and actual sandbox-key tenant (default); documented above for the main agent.
